subject: Trial visibility runbook and POC KPI assignment
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ari Henderson <ari@zephrtech.com>, Danielle Park <danielle.park@zephrtech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Trial visibility runbook and POC KPI assignment

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment across scope. Per our conversation, I put together a concise visibility runbook and an execution sketch so both teams can land the POC observability and acceptance checks quickly. See summary and next steps below.

One-line goal: Prove the trial can run under realistic traffic for two critical flows (document ingestion + API-based chat) while giving ZephrTech the visibility needed to evaluate reliability and cost.

Proposed success signals (we'll refine after instrumentation):
- End-to-end 95th percentile latency for chat API < 300ms (tail under load)
- Error rate (5xx or model runtime failures) < 0.05% sustained
- Model throughput: sustain 120 reqs/min with 99% of requests < 1s queue time
- KV / prefix cache hit rate >= 70% for ingestion-heavy scenarios
- Traceable end-to-end spans across frontend -> gateway -> inference runtime with sampling for 1% of requests
- Automated quality check: pass the curated eval set with no more than a 2% drop vs host model baseline

Observability scope (what we'll deliver):
- Dashboards: Grafana set showing traffic, latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, queue depth, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, cost per 1k tokens (estimated).
- Tracing: Distributed traces instrumented through API gateway and inference runtime (Datadog/Jaeger export) with span tags for customer_id, request_id, model_variant.
- Logs: Structured request/response logs (redacted prompts) streamed to S3 (or GCS) with retention 30d.
- Alerts: Pager-duty on high error-rate and queue growth; Slack channel for visibility alerts.

Owners and tempo:
- Mina Haddad (redwood) — technical lead for instrumentation and acceptance checks (this thread owner).
- Karthik Iyer (redwood) — trial coordinator and timeline owner; will manage weekly syncs and stakeholder updates.
- Marissa Cole (redwood) — client success lead for ZephrTech and primary contact for feature/ops questions.

Timeline (target):
- Day 0 (this week): Agree final success signals and share credentials for staging project + dataset samples.
- Day 3: Instrumentation checklist completed (metrics and trace spans wired, log export configured).
- Day 7: Baseline run + smoke dashboards; initial data ingestion of sample corpus.
- Day 14: Load sweep and acceptance test; iterate on tuning (batching/cache/quantization suggestions).
- Day 21: Consolidated results, go/no-go decision and next steps (Dedicated or further pilot).

Attachments: I attached a compact POC visibility template (poc-visibility-template.xlsx) and a signal-mapping CSV that maps required metrics to dashboard panels and alert rules. I'll also push a starter Grafana dashboard JSON after we confirm AWS/GCP details.

Ask: Please confirm the success signals above, share a staging API key and short sample payloads (s3 link or sample docs), and confirm who from your engineering team will accept instrumentation access.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Trial visibility runbook and POC KPI assignment

Thanks, Mina — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) For the "end-to-end 95th percentile < 300ms" item, is that measured from our client SDK call to the final response, or from the gateway to inference only? We want to set expectations correctly.
2) Could you confirm what will be redacted in the exported logs? We handle sensitive doc content and need PI redaction to be explicit.
3) Our infra lead (Ari) will want GPU utilization and model memory footprint sampled at 10s resolution — does the dashboard template support that granularity?

We can provide a staging API key and a small sample corpus (5 docs) today. I'll loop in Ari on the instrumentation access; he's ok to be the primary SRE contact.

Danielle

Great questions — quick answers and commitments from the Redwood side: 

- Measurement window for p95: we'll measure end-to-end from the ZephrTech client SDK call to the final response for trial reporting, and we will also publish the internal gateway->inference breakdown panels so you can see where time is spent.
- Logs: Redwood will redact prompt text and any detected PII per our standard redaction rules. We'll provide the redaction spec and a sample exported log for review before the trial begins.
- Granularity: Grafana panels can surface 10s-sampled GPU metrics; we'll wire the runtime exporter (nvidia-smi/prom exporter) to the staging cluster.

Operational owner assignments (confirmed):
- Mina Haddad: instrumentation and acceptance tests (technical lead).
- Karthik Iyer: timeline, weekly checkpoints, liaison for billing/contract items.
- Marissa Cole: CSM contact for ZephrTech — will manage cadence and internal comms.

Working plan: I'll create a shared Drive folder and a short checklist doc. Mina, can you start the instrumentation checklist and drop the starter Grafana JSON there? Marissa, I'll book a 30-minute weekly sync for Fridays (10:00 PT) starting next week; will invite ZephrTech.

Attachments we'll push to the Drive: grafana-trial-dashboards.json (starter panels), poc-visibility-template.xlsx, signal-mapping.csv.

Karthik

Appreciate the clear plan. A couple of engineering notes from my side before Mina wires instrumentation: 

- Please include a 99th percentile latency panel and a simple heatmap of tail latency by hour — our traffic spikes in short bursts and the 99th will matter.
- Add a panel for queue growth and a derived metric showing "time-in-queue" for requests waiting for inference. If queue time exceeds 1s for >1% of requests in a 5m window, we want an alert.
- For log exports: we prefer logs land in our S3 bucket (s3://zephrtech-trial-logs) with role-based write permissions. We'll provide a write-only IAM role.
- One more success criterion request: include a cost-signal so we can see estimated token spend / day under baseline load (helpful for procurement).

We confirm staging API key and sample corpus; Danielle will send the manifest. We'll have our SRE (myself) accept instrumentation access tomorrow.

Agree to the timeline; please go ahead and drop the Drive folder and starter dashboards. Looking forward to the first baseline run.

Best,
Ari Henderson
SRE Lead, ZephrTech
